name: 62-env-schema-check
prompt:
Write an executable shell script checkenv.sh, run as `./checkenv.sh <schema> <envfile>`, that validates an env file against a schema. schema.txt, good.env and bad.env are in the directory to try it on; it will also be run against an env file you have not seen.
The schema has one key per line as `<KEY> <type> <required|optional>`, with fields separated by whitespace; type is `int`, `bool` or `str`. The env file has `KEY=VALUE` lines. In both files a blank line, and a line whose first non-whitespace character is `#`, is ignored, and whitespace around a key and around a value is not part of it. A `#` anywhere else is an ordinary character, the value runs to the end of the line, a value may itself contain `=` (the key ends at the first one), and an env-file line with no `=` at all is ignored.
Six rules:
1. Work through the schema keys in the order the schema lists them. A required key that the env file does not set prints `missing: KEY`; an optional one that is not set prints nothing.
2. A key that is set but whose value does not match its type prints `bad: KEY=VALUE`, with VALUE the value as it will be used. `int` is an optional minus sign and one or more digits; `bool` is exactly `true` or `false` in lower case; `str` is any non-empty value.
3. After every schema key has been considered, each key the env file sets that the schema does not mention prints `unknown: KEY`, in the order those keys first appear in the env file.
4. A key set more than once in the env file takes its last value and is reported at most once.
5. Exit 0 when there is nothing to print and exit 1 when there is.
6. Findings go to stdout, one per line, and the script prints nothing else.
Run it on both supplied env files before you finish.

files.schema.txt:
# service configuration
PORT int required
DEBUG bool optional
NAME str required
RETRIES int optional
URL str optional
files.bad.env:
PORT = 80x80
DEBUG=TRUE
EXTRA=1
NAME=
# a comment
RETRIES=-3
PORT=9090
COLOR=red
files..eval/schema.txt:
# service configuration
PORT int required
DEBUG bool optional
NAME str required
RETRIES int optional
URL str optional

check:
set -u
fail() { echo "FAIL: $1"; exit 1; }
test -x checkenv.sh || fail 'checkenv.sh is missing or not executable'
cmp schema.txt .eval/schema.txt || fail 'schema.txt was modified'
out=$(./checkenv.sh schema.txt good.env); rc=$?
test "$rc" = 0 || fail "good.env exited $rc, want 0"
test -z "$out" || fail "good.env printed: $out"
cat > .want_bad <<'WB_EOF'
bad: DEBUG=TRUE
bad: NAME=
unknown: EXTRA
unknown: COLOR
WB_EOF
./checkenv.sh schema.txt bad.env > .got_bad; rc=$?
test "$rc" = 1 || fail "bad.env exited $rc, want 1"
cmp .got_bad .want_bad || { echo '--- got ---'; cat .got_bad; echo '--- want ---'; cat .want_bad; fail 'bad.env output'; }
cat > .third.env <<'T_EOF'
NAME=hello world
RETRIES=abc
DEBUG=true
T_EOF
cat > .want_third <<'WT_EOF'
missing: PORT
bad: RETRIES=abc
WT_EOF
./checkenv.sh schema.txt .third.env > .got_third; rc=$?
test "$rc" = 1 || fail "third fixture exited $rc, want 1"
cmp .got_third .want_third || { echo '--- got ---'; cat .got_third; echo '--- want ---'; cat .want_third; fail 'third fixture output'; }
cat > .fourth.env <<'F_EOF'
# only the KEY=VALUE lines below have meaning
PORT=0x1
URL=http://x/y?a=b#frag
NAME=n # not a comment
no_equals_line
DEBUG=true
F_EOF
cat > .want_fourth <<'WF_EOF'
bad: PORT=0x1
WF_EOF
./checkenv.sh schema.txt .fourth.env > .got_fourth; rc=$?
test "$rc" = 1 || fail "fourth fixture exited $rc, want 1"
cmp .got_fourth .want_fourth || { echo '--- got ---'; cat .got_fourth; echo '--- want ---'; cat .want_fourth; fail 'fourth fixture output'; }
exit 0
